verses.1: Having sent off Shatrughna, Rama, accompanied by his two brothers, happily rejoiced while ruling the kingdom righteously.
verses.2: Then, after a few days, an old Brahmin citizen, holding his dead child, approached the royal gate.
verses.3: Weeping, he uttered various words filled with affection and sorrow, repeatedly exclaiming, "O son, O son!"
verses.4: He lamented, "What evil deed did I commit in a previous birth that I now see you, my only son, having met your death?"
verses.5: The child, though five thousand years old, had not yet reached youth and met an untimely death, causing great sorrow to the speaker.
verses.6: The speaker and the mother will undoubtedly die within a few days due to the grief over the son's death.
verses.7: The speaker asserts that he does not recall ever speaking an untruth, committing violence, or performing any sin against any living being.
verses.8: The speaker wonders what sin he committed that his son, still a child, has died without fulfilling his duties to his ancestors.
verses.9: The speaker states that he has never before seen or heard of such a terrible sight as the untimely death of those in Rama's kingdom.
verses.10: There is no doubt that Rama has committed some great sin, just as death has come upon the children living in his kingdom.
verses.11: Indeed, children in other kingdoms do not fear death, so O King, you must revive this child who has fallen under the sway of death.
verses.12: I will die at the king's gate with my wife, like a helpless person, and then, O Rama, having incurred the sin of killing a Brahmin, you may be happy.
verses.13: O King, accompanied by your brothers, you will obtain a long life; O greatly powerful one, we have lived happily in your kingdom until now.
verses.14: But this misfortune has now befallen us, O Rama, who are under your control, as we have fallen under the sway of time, and indeed, our happiness is now very little.
verses.15: Now, this kingdom of the great Ikshvakus, having obtained Rama as its protector, is certainly causing the death of children.
verses.16: Indeed, subjects not protected according to law perish due to the king's faults, and when the king is ill-behaved, people die untimely deaths.
verses.17: Or when people commit improper acts in cities and districts, and there is no protection, then there is fear caused by the times.
verses.18: It is very clear that there will be no doubt of a king's fault in the city and the district, and therefore, this child-killing is indeed due to that.
verses.19: Thus, repeatedly importuning the king with various kinds of words, the father, deeply distressed, clasps his son. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 73 ।। Thus ends the seventy-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
